newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate rises to 7.30/40 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate rises to 7.30/40 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to 7.30/40 percent on Monday, supported by bids by foreign banks and finance companies seeking fresh funds, dealers said.
The rate closed at 5.9/6.0 percent on Friday.
"The overnight started at 6.20 percent but shot up to 7.30 as there were not many offers," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "Foreigners and finance houses are believed to be short."
He said trading volumes were small due to lack of lenders.
Earlier, interbank rates remained stable in thin activity as lenders were wary of lending any lower amid persistent rumour of a new long-term government bond issue, dealers said.
One-week money was at 6.9/7.0 percent against 7.00/10 on Friday, while two-week and three-week were quoted around Friday's 7.10/20 and 7.20/30 percent respectively.
One-month money at 7.25/30 percent, three-month at 7.35/40 and six-month at 7.40/45, were all unchanged.
Dealers said they expected rates to hover at current levels with players continuing to await announcement of a new bond issue.
Speculation has been rife that Bank Negara will issue new Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) to roll over maturing bonds. A 900-million ringgit issue will mature on May 15.
In addition, there will be a maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday, dealers said.
The central bank said it will issue Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Wednesday.
"That still leave a net inflow of 900 million ringgit this week," said one dealer.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher but volume was thin.
At 0830 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.70, or an implied yield of 7.30 percent.
December and March 1998 were also up one each to 92.70 and 92.65, or 7.30 and 7.35 percent respectively.
